messages:
sam: Quick question — prototyping a Console flow to surface per-route SLOs and alert policies. Proposal: allow teams to attach a notify-policy + runbook link per route, with defaults inherited from service level. Want opinions on ownership and noise controls.

maria: Are we planning per-tenant overrides too or just per-route? sounds like explosion risk.

devon: per-tenant overrides yes but opt-in. We should default to 'monitor-only' alerts (no paging) and let teams opt into pages.

tasha: :100: agree on monitor-only. Also need sampling and a jitter window to reduce fanout. e.g., only notify on X% of violations or rollups every N mins.

nora: Runbooks need to be first-class. If an alert fires, who gets the incident? If it's per-route we need an ownership field that can be a user or an oncall rotation id.

sam: Draft policy shape (sketch):

```
{
  "route_id": "GET /v1/generate",
  "slo": { "window": "30d", "target": 0.999 },
  "alert": {
    "threshold": { "type": "p95_latency", "value_ms": 500 },
    "severity": "page|monitor|ticket",
    "sampling": { "strategy": "percent", "value": 10 },
    "dedupe_key": "service-route",
    "notify_targets": ["#prod-llm-alerts", "rotation:llm-oncall"],
    "runbook_url": "https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/llm-latency"
  }
}
```

sam: Questions: 1) field naming for severity (string vs enum?) 2) should dedupe_key be autogenerated by Console or editable? 3) how to represent 'fallback' notify targets when primary is noisy?

devon: severity should be enum on the backend (so Console can render toggles). Allow editable dedupe_key but default to service-route. For fallback, add tiers with backoff windows.

tasha: Add a 'noise_profile' pointer that links to a tenant-specific suppression policy. Then Console can show expected reduction and false-positive risk.

maria: UX: show a small risk meter and a 'preview' that simulates X days of alerts using historical telemetry before committing policy.

nora: For ownership, accept both user id and rotation id. Also allow 'escalation_matrix' small object with delays.

sam: API proposal snippet for internal discussion:

```
POST /internal/v1/alert-policies
Body: { route_id, policy, dry_run: true }
Response: { policy_id, preview: { estimated_alerts_per_day } }
```

sam: If dry_run returns a high alert rate we should block by default and show remediation suggestions (increase sampling, widen threshold, choose monitor-only).

deploy-bot: deployment redwood-console@release-2026.03.18 succeeded :rocket:

devon: one more thought — telemetry tagging needs to include policy_id so we can track regressions after a rollout.

tasha: agree. also need a way to migrate legacy alert configs into this shape; maybe a one-click import that maps keys and shows conflicts.

maria: ok let's collect actionable items: (1) finalize policy JSON schema, (2) implement dry_run preview API, (3) Console preview UX + risk meter, (4) ownership/escalation fields + rotation integration, (5) migration path for legacy alerts.

sam: I'll open an RFC with the schema and wireframes. tagging @tasha @devon for API and telemetry, @nora for runbooks/ownership. thanks all :pray:
